The allocator is initialized at the start of the region and used in allocate on the parallel for. Repeated const is valid C99. Rejecting the clause as unimplemented is non-conformance. Some uncertainty about allocate/default(none) interaction.

uses_allocators with traits modifier and allocator is the OpenMP 5.2 syntax on target; the allocator is privatized and used in allocate clause on the inner parallel for; default(none) lists a, b, my_alloc, t is private. 'const const' is permitted in C99 and later. The 'unimplemented' refusal is a missing feature, not permitted nonacceptance.

uses_allocators with a traits modifier on target is OpenMP 5.2 syntax. The traits array is const, has constant values and is defined in the same scope as the construct. The allocator is a variable and not in other data-sharing clauses of the target. Duplicate const is allowed in C99 and later. A compiler rejecting the clause as unimplemented fails to accept a conforming program.

uses_allocators with a traits-array modifier and an allocator variable is allowed on target. The traits array is a constant array with constant values defined in the same scope as the construct. The allocator is not in any other data-sharing or map clause on the target. Inside the region my_alloc is available for the allocate clause. Duplicate const qualifiers are legal in C99. A conforming compiler must accept it; refusing with 'unimplemented' is a compiler limitation.
